metaData.originalTitle: 浅谈 AI 超级应用
metaData.title: On AI Super Apps
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the engineering convergence trend of AI evolving from a 'question-answering system' to an 'action system', pointing out that AI is re-engaging with classic software engineering structures such as browsers, file systems, and protocols to build controllable Agent infrastructure.
metaData.summary: Using 'AI Super Apps' as a starting point, the article explores a counterintuitive yet crucial trend in current AI technology evolution: as AI shifts from generating text to executing real-world tasks, it is not bypassing established software engineering systems but instead deeply embracing mature technologies like HTML, browsers, file systems, terminals, Git, and the MCP protocol. By analyzing Codex's distributed Agent workstation architecture (multi-track execution, sandbox isolation, decoupling of control plane and execution plane), Claude Cowork's workflow control, Ralph Loop's long-cycle task mode, the presentation layer debate between Markdown and HTML, Google A2UI's declarative UI approach, and Bun's migration from Zig to Rust, the author argues a core point: the ultimate form of AI is not a smarter model, but an 'action system' constrained and organized by classic engineering structures. The article emphasizes that this seemingly 'regressive' convergence is actually the restoration of order after a complex system matures, and an inevitable path for AI deployment.

mainPoints.point: AI is transitioning from a 'question-answering system' to an 'action system' and must integrate with classic software engineering structures.
mainPoints.explanation: When AI begins to read and write files, control browsers, and execute commands, relying solely on model capabilities is insufficient. It requires mature structures like browsers, file systems, protocols, and sandboxes to constrain and support its actions, ensuring controllability and safety.

mainPoints.point: Products like Codex are building distributed Agent workstations, achieving decoupling of the control plane and execution plane.
mainPoints.explanation: Codex, through multi-track execution modes, sandbox isolation, and mobile control, splits development tasks into execution environments (local/cloud) and control entry points (phone/desktop), allowing humans to orchestrate at key nodes rather than accompany the entire process.

mainPoints.point: The Ralph Loop model addresses context corruption in long tasks through 'stateless loops'.
mainPoints.explanation: This model forces state externalization (persisting to files) and refreshes the Agent instance with each cycle, using deterministic loops to constrain non-deterministic models. It is a key engineering path to overcoming long-context attention decay.

mainPoints.point: The Markdown vs. HTML debate is essentially a rebalancing of machine computational efficiency and human cognitive load.
mainPoints.explanation: Markdown is machine-friendly but causes 'AI brain overload' for humans, while HTML leverages the visual cortex to increase information density. Solutions like A2UI propose a three-layer division: Markdown preserves facts, A2UI expresses intent, and HTML handles presentation.

keyQuotes: AI has not bypassed the old world. It is leveraging the old world to gain a tangible form for entering reality.
Truly mature AI programming is not Vibe Coding, but Spec-driven Porting, Harness-driven Rewrite, and Evidence-based Refactor.
To enable AI to work autonomously for long periods without drifting, one must remain vigilant about the cognitive corrosion that can arise from the accumulation of extremely long contexts.

The fundamental structure of a large language model is ultimately a generation engine based on the probability distribution of massive corpora; to allow this wild horse, full of creativity and danger, to truly enter... the domain, we must forge a highly deterministic, standardized, and universally applicable rigid constraint framework for it.

relatedArticles.title: Deep Dive: Claude Code Source Code
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the reverse-engineered source code of Claude Code, revealing its agent architecture based on Harness Engineering, with a focus on core mechanisms like state persistence, tool scheduling, and the system prompt control plane.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4: Professional Workflows Enter the 'Executable Era'
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: GPT-5.4 marks the leap from conversational assistants to autonomous execution agents, deeply embedding into professional workflows through native computer use, dynamic tool search, and interactive thinking.

relatedArticles.title: Deep Dive: Google Workspace CLI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the architectural design of the Google Workspace CLI (gws), exploring the underlying logic of the transition from "Human-First" to "Agent-First" software interaction and the central role of Rust in the AI toolchain.

relatedArticles.title: On Agent Memory
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the essence, architectural philosophy, and governance challenges of AI Agent memory systems, arguing that true memory is not simple storage and retrieval, but the continuous reinterpretation, hierarchical governance, and skill solidification of past experiences, while critiquing the common misconception of equating RAG or long context with memory.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: The Essence of Agent Memory Architecture
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the architectural essence of Agent Memory systems, arguing that the core challenge lies in governance rather than capacity, and systematically proposes a complete design framework comprising four modeling objects, a six-dimensional basic memory unit, and three core links.
